questions.question: If sec A=(17)/(15), then what is the value of cot A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sec A = 17/15

**Formula used:**

Sec θ = H/B

By Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ H² = P² + B²

Where H = hypotenuse ; P = perpendicular

and B = base

**Calculation:**

Sec A = 17/15 = H/B

By Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ H2 = P2 + B2

⇒ 17² = P² + 15²

⇒ P = √(289 - 225)

⇒ P = √64 = 8

So, cot A = B/P 

⇒ 15/8

**∴ The correct answer is 15/8.**

questions.question: If sec x + tan x = 5 and cosec y - cot y = (1)/(3), then find the value of (sec x + cosec y) - (tan x - cot y).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sec x + tan x = 5 and cosec y - cot y = (1)/(3)

**Formula used:**

sec²θ - tan²θ = 1

cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1

a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b)

**Calculation:**

sec x + tan x = 5,

sec2x - tan2x = 1

⇒ (sec x + tan x)(sec x - tan x) = 1

⇒ 5 × (sec x - tan x) = 1

⇒ (sec x - tan x) = 1over5 

Now, cosec y - cot y = (1)/(3)

cosec²y - cot²y = 1

⇒ (cosec y + cot y)(cosec y - cot y) = 1

⇒ (1/3) × (cosec y + cot y) = 1

⇒ cosec y + cot y = 3

Again according to the question,

⇒ (sec x + cosec y) - (tan x - cot y)

⇒ sec x + cosec y - tan x + cot y

⇒ sec x - tan x + cosec y + cot y

⇒ (1)/(5) + 3 = 16over5 = 3.2

**∴ The value of (sec x + cosec y) - (tan x - cot y) is 3.2**

questions.question: If sin α + cos α = (2)/(sqrt3), then what is (tan α + cot α) equal to?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct identity: (sin α + cos α)² = 1 + 2 / (tan α + cot α)

Substitute the given value: (2/√3)² = 1 + 2 / (tan α + cot α)

⇒ 4/3 = 1 + 2 / (tan α + cot α)

⇒ 1/3 = 2 / (tan α + cot α)

⇒ tan α + cot α = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin α + cos α = 2/√3

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2 × a × b

sin² α + cos² α = 1

tan α = sin α / cos α and cot α = cos α / sin α

**Calculations:**

Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (sin α + cos α)² = (2/√3)²

⇒ sin² α + cos² α + 2 × sin α × cos α = 4/3

Substitute sin² α + cos² α = 1:

⇒ 1 + 2 × sin α × cos α = 4/3

⇒ 2 × sin α × cos α = 4/3 − 1

⇒ 2 × sin α × cos α = 1/3

⇒ sin α × cos α = 1/6

Now evaluate (tan α + cot α):

⇒ tan α + cot α = (sin α / cos α) + (cos α / sin α)

⇒ tan α + cot α = (sin² α + cos² α) / (sin α × cos α)

⇒ tan α + cot α = 1 / (sin α × cos α)

Substitute the value of sin α × cos α:

⇒ tan α + cot α = 1 / (1/6)

⇒ tan α + cot α = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin² α + cos² α = 1, sec² α − tan² α = 1, and cosec² α − cot² α = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

tan α = 1 / cot α, sin α = 1 / cosec α, and cos α = 1 / sec α.

Key Shortcut Formula

The expression tan α + cot α frequently simplifies to 1 / (sin α × cos α), which is a direct and standard substitution for trigonometric simplifications.

questions.question: If cosec θ - sin θ = a³, sec θ - cos θ = b³, then a²b² (a² + b²) is equal to
questions.solution:
**Given:**

cosec θ - sin θ = a3

sec θ - cos θ = b³

**Formula Used: **

 
• cosecθ = 1/sinθ
 
• secθ = 1/cosθ
 
• sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
 
• (am)ⁿ = amⁿ
 
• amaⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

 

**Calculation: **

Given that,

cosec θ - sin θ = a³

⇒ 1/sinθ - sinθ = a³

⇒ (1 - sin²θ)/sinθ = a³

⇒ (cos2θ)/sinθ = a3

⇒ **[cos²θ/sin θ]¹/³ = a ** ----(1)

Also, we have sec θ - cos θ = b³ 

⇒ 1/cos θ - cosθ = b³

⇒ (1 - cos²θ)/cosθ = b³

⇒ **[sin²θ/cos θ]¹/³ = b ** -----(2)

Now, the value of a2b2 (a2 + b2) 

Using equation (1) & (2)

⇒ [(cos²θ)/(sin θ)]²/³[(sin²θ)/(cos θ)]²/³[((cos²θ)/(sin θ))²/³+((sin²θ)/(cos θ))²/³]

⇒ [(cos²θ)/(sin θ)times (sin²θ)/(cos θ)]²/³[(frac{cos⁴/³θ}{sin²/³ θ})+(frac{sin⁴/³θ}{cos²/³ θ})^{}]

⇒ cos²/³θ sin²/³θ [frac{cos²θ+sin²θ}{sin²/³θ cos²/³θ}]

⇒ sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

⇒ a2b2 (a2 + b2) = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1 **

questions.question:
Using the measurements given in the following figure, the value of (sin phi+tan theta)/(sin phi−tan theta) is ________.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58e0532b059d8948f29c62fa8989dfc9d02714366f003026b3ac11355e4f5b1b.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58e0532b059d8948f29c62fa8989dfc9d02714366f003026b3ac11355e4f5b1b.png] 

**Concept used:**

Pythagoras theorem, 

Sum of square of the other sides of the right-angled triangle is equal to the square of the hypotenuse.

**Calculations:**

According to question,

DC = √(13² - 12²) = √(169 - 144) = √25 = 5

sinphi = DC/BD = 5/13

Let a line from D perpendicular to line AB at E,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0efeb2f4bf45fb150b86bb3cf3ee2256b236018008844f311e5abef875f809a.png] 

Then AE = AB - DC = 14 - 5 = 9

tan theta = DE/AE = BC/AE = 12/9 = 4/3

Now, (sinphi + tantheta)/(sinphi - tantheta)

= (frac{5)/(13)+(4)/(3)}{(5)/(13)-(4)/(3)}

= - 67/37

**Hence, The Required value is - 67/37.**

questions.question: (sin(90^circ-x)cosec(90^circ-x))/(1+tan²(90^circ-x)) ?
questions.solution:
**Formula Used:**

sin (90 - θ) = cos θ 

tan (90 - θ) = cot θ 

cosec (90 - θ) = sec θ 

sec2θ - 1 = tan2θ ⇒ 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ 

1/(cosec θ) = sin θ 

**Calculation:**

(sin(90^circ-x)cosec(90^circ-x))/(1+tan²(90^circ-x))

By using the above formula 

⇒ 1/(1 + cot²x)

⇒ 1/cosec²x

⇒ sin²x

∴ (sin(90^circ-x)cosec(90^circ-x))/(1+tan²(90^circ-x)) = sin2x
